clue.text: Film valet Valentino sacked

indicators.note: sacked suggests something ransacked and thrown into disorder, so the two names are jumbled together

explanation.surface: A film star's manservant loses his job working for Rudolph Valentino.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sacked' looks like the valet's dismissal but tells you to rearrange all fourteen letters of VALET VALENTINO.
explanation.definitionFit: The 1944 picture starring Elizabeth Taylor as a girl who rides in the Grand National is a film.

clue.text: Oddly no new direction for bygone film?

definitions.meaning: the odd letters of 'no new' are N, N and W, the compass abbreviation for a point between north and north-west; this sense is that point written out in full
an old film: Hitchcock's 1959 thriller, whose actual title is North by Northwest

explanation.surface: A puzzle about an old movie that oddly changed course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Oddly' picks letters 1, 3 and 5 of NO NEW, giving NNW; the answer is that abbreviation spelt out. The blog notes the film is properly North by Northwest, so the second sense is loose.
explanation.definitionFit: Hitchcock's thriller starring Cary Grant is a famous old picture whose title closely resembles this compass bearing.

clue.text: Bowl along right round North Dakota lake

indicators.note: round means the word for right goes around the other pieces

parts.note: right in the sense of correct is true
ND is the US postal abbreviation for North Dakota
L is the standard abbreviation for lake on maps

explanation.surface: A cricket bowler sends the ball past a lake in North Dakota.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bowl' suggests cricket, but here it means to roll or move along on wheels.
explanation.definitionFit: To trundle is to move or roll along slowly and heavily, as a ball or cart does.

clue.text: Painting interior of woman's extension

definitions.meaning: a picture by a great European artist of the period before about 1800
the inside letters of 'woman' are O, M and A; read as abbreviations, O is old and MA is Master (of Arts), and this sense is those abbreviations written out in full

explanation.surface: Someone is decorating the inside of a woman's new extension to her house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'extension' means expansion of an abbreviation: OMA, the middle of WOMAN, expanded as O (old) and MA (Master of Arts). 'Painting' looks like decorating the house, but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A canvas by a renowned artist such as Rembrandt or Titian is called by this term.

clue.text: Hint of troubled soul in LA

indicators.note: troubled means disturbed or agitated, so these letters are stirred into a new order

explanation.surface: A suggestion that a person in Los Angeles has a troubled soul.
explanation.walkthrough: 'troubled' rearranges SOUL IN LA.
explanation.definitionFit: An allusion is an indirect reference, which is a kind of hint.

clue.text: Part of the gay Ovidian's uphill journey

indicators.note: uphill in a down clue means the run is read from bottom to top
part of means the letters are a stretch taken from inside the following words

explanation.surface: A section of the joyful Roman poet's climb up a hill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Part of' takes EGAYOV from thE GAY OVidian's, and 'uphill' reads it bottom to top in this down light.
explanation.definitionFit: A voyage is a long journey, especially one made by sea.

clue.text: Furious little girl wearing hat

indicators.note: wearing means the girl has the hat around her, so she sits inside it

parts.note: lid is slang for a hat
Vi is a short form of the girl's name Violet

explanation.surface: A small child loses her temper while wearing a hat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wearing' signals the girl sits inside the hat; Vi is a common short form of Violet.
explanation.definitionFit: Livid means extremely angry, a synonym of furious.

clue.text: Stores spread around Rome and Pisa, not opening Sundays

indicators.note: spread around means the letters are scattered into a new arrangement
not opening tells us the shop letter for Sundays is shut out of the city name

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for Sunday

explanation.surface: Shops scattered around two Italian cities stay shut on Sundays.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not opening Sundays' shuts S out of the second city, leaving PIA; 'spread around' then mixes those letters with the first city's.
explanation.definitionFit: Emporia, the plural of emporium, are large shops or trading places.

clue.text: Film girl going up and down rising river on a Chester outing

indicators.note: going up and down says the name reads the same in either direction in this down light

parts.note: Ada is a girl's name

indicators.note: rising in a down light means the river's name is read upwards

parts.note: the Tay is a Scottish river

indicators.note: outing suggests the letters being taken out and rearranged

explanation.surface: A girl travels on a river trip during a day out at Chester.
explanation.walkthrough: ADA reads the same both ways; 'rising' turns TAY into YAT; 'outing' rearranges A CHESTER into THERACES. Chester has a well-known racecourse, which feeds the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a 1937 Marx Brothers film comedy.

clue.text: Song and dance about university retirement

parts.note: round means about, as in 'round the house'

indicators.note: retirement means the university's name goes backwards, retreating

parts.note: Yale is an American university

explanation.surface: A professor celebrates leaving the university with singing and dancing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retirement' turns YALE back to ELAY.
explanation.definitionFit: A roundelay is a short song with a refrain, and also a circle dance.

clue.text: Flat race leader dropped out of very fast

indicators.note: dropped out of means that letter is removed from the word for fast

parts.note: rapid means fast

indicators.note: leader means the opening letter of the word race

explanation.surface: The front-runner pulls out of a very quick race.
explanation.walkthrough: 'race leader' is R, and 'dropped out of' removes it from RAPID, leaving APID.
explanation.definitionFit: Vapid means dull and lifeless, which is what flat means of a performance or conversation.

clue.text: Horse and cart back to front? It's monstrous

parts.note: H is slang for heroin, which is also called horse

indicators.note: back to front means the last letter of the cart word moves to its front

parts.note: a dray is a low cart for heavy loads

explanation.surface: A horse and cart are hitched the wrong way round.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back to front' moves the Y of DRAY to the front, giving YDRA. 'It's monstrous' defines a monster: the many-headed serpent of Greek myth.
explanation.definitionFit: The Hydra was a many-headed monster of Greek legend, killed by Hercules.

clue.text: Cheese straw's started to become old hat

indicators.note: started means only the beginning letter of straw's is used

parts.note: to age is to become old
a derby is a bowler hat

explanation.surface: A straw hat goes out of fashion.
explanation.walkthrough: SAGE DERBY is an English cheese marbled green with sage.
explanation.definitionFit: Sage Derby is a type of English cheese flavoured with sage.

clue.text: Passed open hole all right

parts.note: overt means open, not hidden
O is a hole by its shape
OK means all right

explanation.surface: A golfer finds an open hole and is satisfied.
explanation.definitionFit: To have overtaken someone is to have passed them on the road.

clue.text: Mongrel incorporating a new genetic variation

indicators.note: incorporating means the dog word takes the other letters into itself

parts.note: a mutt is a mongrel dog

explanation.surface: A crossbreed dog that carries a new genetic change.
explanation.walkthrough: 'incorporating' puts A and N inside MUTT.
explanation.definitionFit: A mutant is an organism showing a genetic change, that is, a variant produced by mutation.

clue.text: Roughly a hundred keeping name secret

indicators.note: keeping means the scrambled letters hold the abbreviation inside them
roughly means treated roughly and so put out of order

explanation.surface: Around a hundred people keep a person's name confidential.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Roughly' looks like 'approximately', but it rearranges A HUNDRED; 'keeping' puts N inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Underhand means done in secret, sly and deceitful.

clue.text: Growths worrying Kate and Rose

indicators.note: worrying means troubling or shaking up, so the names are jumbled

explanation.surface: Something growing is troubling two women.
explanation.walkthrough: 'worrying' rearranges KATE and ROSE.
explanation.definitionFit: Oak trees are things that grow, so they are growths in a loose sense.

clue.text: Party right to the end in Tennessee bar

indicators.note: in means the party word sits inside the state abbreviation

parts.note: TN is the US postal abbreviation for Tennessee

indicators.note: to the end says the letter for right is moved to the back of the party word

parts.note: a rave is a party

explanation.surface: Someone parties until closing time in a Tennessee bar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'right to the end' moves the R of RAVE to the back, giving AVER, which goes 'in' TN.
explanation.definitionFit: A tavern is a pub or inn, that is, a bar.

clue.text: Italian city lights, initially hypnotic

parts.note: Verona is a city in northern Italy

indicators.note: initially means only the first letter of lights is used

explanation.surface: The lights of an Italian city at night have a mesmerising effect.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hypnotic' is a noun here, a sleep-inducing drug: Veronal was a barbiturate.
explanation.definitionFit: Veronal was the trade name of barbital, a sleeping drug, which is a hypnotic in the medical sense.

clue.text: Open club in 2011, if club then not open

definitions.meaning: the golf club, Royal St George's in this Kent town, that hosted the British Open championship in 2011
a club version of this snack is closed, with bread on top, unlike an open one

explanation.surface: A golf club's Open hosting and whether the club is open.
explanation.walkthrough: Royal St George's, a golf course in a Kent town, hosted the 2011 Open Championship. A club sandwich has a top slice of bread, so it is not open.
explanation.definitionFit: The golf course is at this town in Kent, and the word also names bread with a filling.

clue.text: Disbeliever took the initiative, providing part of UK's upturn

indicators.note: upturn in a down light means the whole string is read from bottom to top

parts.note: led means took the initiative
if means providing, as in 'providing that'
NI is Northern Ireland, part of the UK

explanation.surface: Someone who doubts that a leader revived the UK's economy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upturn' turns LEDIFNI, read upwards, into INFIDEL.
explanation.definitionFit: An infidel is someone who does not believe in a given religion.

clue.text: Poet no expert in advertising

indicators.note: no means the expert word is absent from the advertising word

parts.note: promotion is advertising
a pro is an expert

explanation.surface: A poet who is no good at advertising.
explanation.walkthrough: Andrew Motion was the UK's Poet Laureate from 1999 to 2009.
explanation.definitionFit: Andrew Motion is an English poet, Poet Laureate from 1999 to 2009.

clue.text: Fellow in RAF wrote about what he took part in?

indicators.note: in means the abbreviation goes inside the rearranged letters
about means the letters are moved around

explanation.surface: An airman wrote about the wartime campaign he took part in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' signals the anagram and 'in' the insertion. The definition reads on from the wordplay: what an RAF fellow took part in, the national wartime push.
explanation.definitionFit: The war effort was the whole national contribution to fighting a war, which an RAF airman shared in.

clue.text: Fine hotel for a cat

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for fine, as on pencils
the Ritz is a famous London hotel

explanation.surface: A good hotel for a cat.
explanation.walkthrough: Fritz the Cat is a well-known cartoon character.
explanation.definitionFit: Fritz the Cat is a cartoon character, so this name belongs to a well-known cat.

clue.text: Toke finally taken from joint? Pass on to another

indicators.note: taken from means that letter is removed from the joint word

parts.note: a reefer is a cannabis joint

indicators.note: finally means the last letter of toke

explanation.surface: A smoker takes a last drag on a joint and passes it to someone else.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Toke finally' is E, and 'taken from' removes one E from REEFER.
explanation.definitionFit: To refer a matter is to pass it on to someone else to deal with.

clue.text: Wrong road for the mountain

parts.note: a sin is a wrong
the A1 is Britain's longest road, written AI with the letter I for one

explanation.surface: Taking the wrong road towards the mountain.
explanation.walkthrough: The A1 is the main road from London to Edinburgh; crosswords write it AI.
explanation.definitionFit: Sinai is the biblical mountain where Moses received the commandments.

clue.text: Language from bridge player shortly to end up in one club doubled

indicators.note: in means the bridge player and the landing word go inside the doubled pair
doubled means the pair of letters is written twice

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
C is the abbreviation for clubs in card games
E is East, one of the four bridge players, written shortly
to land is to end up somewhere

explanation.surface: A bridge player's remark about bidding one club and being doubled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'doubled' makes ICIC from I and C, and 'in' puts E and LAND inside it. In bridge, 'doubled' is also a bid, which shapes the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Icelandic is the language spoken in Iceland.

clue.text: Very angry son goes off film

parts.note: blazing means furious
addles means goes bad, as eggs do

explanation.surface: A furious son storms off out of the cinema.
explanation.walkthrough: 'goes off' looks like leaving, but means going rotten: ADDLES.
explanation.definitionFit: Blazing Saddles is Mel Brooks's 1974 Western comedy film.
